name: Diphenhydramine
summary: Sedating first-generation antihistamine with potent anticholinergic effects — used for allergies, motion sickness, insomnia, and acute dystonia.
mechanism: Competitive H1 antagonist that crosses the blood-brain barrier, producing sedation; also antimuscarinic.

dosing.maxDose: 300 mg/day (OTC oral); up to 400 mg/day parenteral
dosing.renalAdjustment: No standard adjustment; caution in renal impairment

safety.pregnancy: Widely used; no major teratogenicity demonstrated, but avoid routine use near term
safety.lactation: Excreted in breast milk; may sedate the infant — avoid routine use
warnings: Marked sedation — avoid driving and machinery
Anticholinergic burden — avoid in elderly (falls, confusion), narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hyperplasia
Do not use as a sleep aid in children under 2 years (FDA warning)
monitoring: Anticholinergic symptoms (dry mouth, urinary retention, confusion)
safety.overdose: Anticholinergic toxidrome — agitation, delirium, seizures, hyperthermia, arrhythmias; can be life-threatening; supportive care (physostigmine in severe cases, specialist setting)

clinicalPearls: Sedation and anticholinergic action are therapeutic in motion sickness and insomnia but are liabilities in the elderly (Beers criteria)
IV diphenhydramine is the classic antidote for acute dystonic reactions
good: Strong sedation and anticholinergic action — night pruritus, motion sickness, dystonia
bad: Elderly, glaucoma, prostatic hyperplasia, drivers, and children under 2
